evidence.excerpt: The effect of oven ageing at 80 °C for periods of 0, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days on the properties of two mLLDPE cast films was investigated to assess fitness for shelf-life-extended food packaging. Films were evaluated by DSC (crystallinity, melting peak), tensile testing (yield stress, elongation at break), and seal strength at a fixed jaw temperature of 115 °C. After 28 days, crystallinity increased by 3.1–4.7 percentage points in both grades, consistent with post-crystallisation. Yield stress rose by 8–12 %, while elongation at break declined from 620 % to 490–530 %, indicating embrittlement. Seal strength dropped by 12–17 % relative to the unaged films, attributed to increased crystallinity at the film surface reducing interdiffusion during sealing. Oxidation induction time measured by DSC-OIT at 200 °C under oxygen remained above 25 min for both grades after 28 days, indicating that the primary antioxidant package was not depleted. The results suggest a conservative shelf life of 18 months for sealed rolls stored below 35 °C.
